title: Encoding, Buffering and Safe Resource Management
learningObjectives: Choose UTF-8 explicitly when encoding portable text files
Distinguish Java character counts from encoded byte lengths
Process large files incrementally instead of loading all content
Use buffering and structured cleanup for reliable file operations
Verify that text survives an encode and decode round trip

understand.concept: Text is encoded as bytes using a charset. The same characters can produce different bytes under different encodings. Use UTF-8 explicitly, process large content incrementally and use try-with-resources.
understand.whyItMatters: Encoding, Buffering and Safe Resource Management helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain.
understand.analogy: Treat the concept as a clearly labeled tool for one programming responsibility.
understand.analogyLimit: Actual behavior is defined by Java language rules and API contracts.

explain.narrative:
## Characters and bytes are not interchangeable

A Java `String` represents text as UTF-16 code units; a file or network stream carries bytes. A charset defines how characters are encoded into bytes and decoded back. UTF-8 uses a variable number of bytes per Unicode code point, so the number of Java string code units is not generally the same as the number of UTF-8 bytes.

## Choose and apply an explicit charset

Use `StandardCharsets.UTF_8` with byte/string conversions and file APIs when UTF-8 is the agreed format. Encoding and decoding must use compatible charsets. Decoding arbitrary bytes with the wrong charset can produce replacement characters or incorrect text even when the original bytes were valid.

## Buffer large content and manage resources

For large files, read and write in chunks or lines rather than loading the entire file into memory. Buffered wrappers reduce repeated low-level operations. Use try-with-resources for owned readers, writers and streams; closing a wrapper also closes the wrapped resource. Handle malformed input according to the application's policy rather than silently assuming every byte sequence is valid text.

## Verify encoding behavior

Compare ASCII, accented characters and non-Latin text. Check both the restored string and the encoded byte length. Test an empty file, a large file, a malformed byte sequence and an I/O failure. For interchange formats, document the charset and any byte-order mark or newline expectations so different systems interpret the data consistently.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { byte[] bytes = "café".getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8); System.out.println(bytes.length); } }
examples.explanation: UTF-8 encodes the string into five bytes.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String restored = new String("Code".getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8), java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8); System.out.println(restored); } }
examples.explanation: Decodes bytes using the same explicit charset.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println("A".length() + ":" + "é".getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length); } }
examples.explanation: Shows that a Java String length and its UTF-8 byte count are different measures.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var writer = new java.io.StringWriter(); var buffered = new java.io.BufferedWriter(writer)) { buffered.write("safe"); buffered.flush(); System.out.println(writer); } } }

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println("Process chunks instead of loading a very large file at once"); } }
examples.expectedOutput: Process chunks instead of loading a very large file at once
examples.explanation: States the memory-safety principle for large streams.

practise.guidedTask: Encode a string containing ASCII and non-ASCII characters as UTF-8 bytes, decode it again and compare the original and restored strings.
practise.independentTask: Build a large-file processor that reads and writes buffered text incrementally using UTF-8 rather than loading the whole file into memory.
hints: Use the same explicitly selected charset when encoding and decoding; UTF-8 is common but should be part of the format contract.
String.length() counts UTF-16 code units, not UTF-8 bytes or necessarily Unicode code points.
Process large data incrementally and test non-ASCII text, malformed bytes and resource cleanup.
practise.challenge: Measure and explain the difference between String.length() and UTF-8 byte length for ASCII, accented and Telugu text; verify cleanup on failure.

options: A character encoding that maps Unicode text to bytes
A Java collection type
A file compression algorithm
A network protocol for Java compilation
questions.answer: A character encoding that maps Unicode text to bytes
questions.explanation: UTF-8 defines how Unicode text is encoded into a sequence of bytes and decoded back into characters.

questions.prompt: Why can a character count differ from a byte count?
options: Some characters require multiple bytes in UTF-8
Every character always uses exactly 8 bytes
Bytes include file names
Java strings store only ASCII
questions.answer: Some characters require multiple bytes in UTF-8
questions.explanation: UTF-8 is variable-width: some code points need multiple bytes, so character counts and encoded byte counts can differ.

questions.prompt: Which practice is best for very large text files?
options: Process the content incrementally with buffered readers
Always read the entire file into one String
Convert the file to an int array
Skip resource closure
questions.answer: Process the content incrementally with buffered readers
questions.explanation: Incremental buffered processing avoids loading an entire large file into memory at once.

questions.prompt: What does try-with-resources guarantee for an AutoCloseable resource?
options: A close attempt on scope exit, including exceptional exit
Successful disk writes in every circumstance
No IOException can occur
The file is automatically backed up
questions.answer: A close attempt on scope exit, including exceptional exit
questions.explanation: Try-with-resources attempts to close an AutoCloseable resource when control exits the statement, including when the body throws.

options: To make text interpretation consistent across environments
To make every character one byte
To avoid using streams
To force alphabetical sorting
questions.answer: To make text interpretation consistent across environments
questions.explanation: An explicit UTF-8 contract prevents machines with different default charsets from interpreting the same file differently.
